findings.detail: A script containing `some-command >& /dev/null` passes without an exception, although Bash redirects both stdout and stderr to /dev/null. Likewise, `some-command >& diagnostics.log` bypasses the retained-diagnostics rule. Both are sibling spellings of redirects the guard rejects.
findings.evidence: Neither matcher recognizes `>&` followed by a filename: the discard expression covers 2>, &>, and > /dev/null 2>&1; the capture expression covers 2>&1, 2>file, and &>. The installed Bash manual's 'Redirecting Standard Output and Standard Error' section explicitly defines >&word and &>word as equivalent.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: >&file bypasses both redirect checks

findings.detail: Replacing a continued backslash with a space changes shell tokens. For the two physical lines `some-command 2\` and `>/dev/null`, Bash sees `some-command 2>/dev/null`, but the guard sees `some-command 2 >/dev/null`. Neither matcher rejects the latter, so an unreasoned stderr discard passes. Splitting `2>&1` between `>` and `&` similarly bypasses the capture check.
findings.evidence: Line 137 substitutes a literal space for the trailing backslash before concatenating the next line. The installed Bash manual's quoting section states that an unquoted backslash-newline pair is removed, not replaced with whitespace. The existing continued-discard sample splits between arguments and therefore does not exercise continuation inside a redirect token.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: continuation joining changes redirect tokens

findings.detail: A blank or comment-only line after a continuation leaves output_line pending across a real command boundary. For example, `some-command 2>/dev/null \`, followed by a blank line, then `true # error-output-allow: separate probe`, is accepted. Bash terminates the first command at the blank line, so its discard has no exception; the guard incorrectly borrows the later command's reason.
findings.evidence: Line 134 skips blank and comment-only lines before the pending logical line can be checked or cleared. The next nonempty line is appended at line 136, and its marker makes check_output return at line 64 before recording the earlier discard. The next-line-reason test has no pending continuation and misses this branch.
findings.title: Validator gaps: skipped lines transfer exceptions between commands
